clips.linkedin:
Your AI can check what Google says about your brand every fortnight and tell you what's changed.

DemandSphere's September data had AI Overviews on about 82% of the brand searches it tracks. That puts a paragraph Google wrote on the page a prospect sees before a sales call, and in most teams nobody owns it. SEO has the search, brand has the message and PR has the sources it cites.

Our view is that the head of brand or comms should own it, with SEO doing the monitoring.

The monitoring is the part to hand over. Give your AI your brand name, your product names and the usual reviews, pricing and competitor searches, and it records each summary and its sources and flags what has moved since the last run.

The full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/google-ai-overviews-brand-searches/ (the podcast voices are AI-generated).
clips.text: Brand searches usually belong to SEO. What the summary says belongs to brand and comms. The sources it cites often belong to PR. Three teams, one paragraph. Which usually means nobody. Our view at Manual Focus is that the head of brand or comms should own the AI Overview on your brand name, with SEO supplying the monitoring. What it says is a reputation question before it's a ranking one.

Your AI can check what Google says about your brand every fortnight and tell you what's changed.

Google now writes an AI Overview on most brand searches, and you can't edit it. What you can do is watch it and fix the sources it reads.

Give your AI a short list of queries. Your company name, your main product names, and your name with reviews, with pricing and against your main competitor. It runs each one and records the summary, the sources Google links beside it and where it sits on the page. Set it to run every fortnight with the same list and it tells you what has moved.

The prompt is in the show notes, with the full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/google-ai-overviews-brand-searches/ (the podcast voices are AI-generated).
clips.text: Get AI on the brand-search check itself. Give it your query list: your company name, your main product names, and your name with reviews, with pricing, and versus your main competitor. It runs each one, records the summary, the sources Google links beside it, and where the summary sits on the page. Set it as a fortnightly routine with the same list, and it tells you what's moved since the last run.
